messages:
noah: Heads-up — ECP negotiated a retroactive rate shift for Q4 with AWS partner. AWS posted partner credits but our reseller mapping didn't pick up the new tier. Seeing negative usage lines + one large debit on our side: INV-20241009 shows a $67,420 adjustment. Can finance ops triage?

olivia: Ack. Can you paste a sample of the invoice lines and the partner change note?

noah: Sample from the invoice CSV I pulled: 
```
invoice_id,customer_id,sku,usage_units,old_rate,new_rate,charge
INV-20241009,CUST-211,ecp-llm-hour,1200,0.085,0.045, -102.00
INV-20241009,CUST-909,ecp-emb-1,50000,0.0006,0.0003,-150.00
INV-20241009,RESELLER-123,partner-fee,1,0.00,0.00,67422.00
```
The negative lines are AWS credits; the large positive line is our ledger absorbing the partner rebate incorrectly. I also uploaded the partner note to S3: s3://redwood/partner-notes/ecp-ratechange-2024-10-09.pdf

eli: looping in the AWS rep I was speaking with — they confirmed a backdated ratecard effective 2024-10-01 and said credits would hit partner account, not marketplace. Looks like their reconciliation file used reseller_id=RESELLER-123 and our mapping table didn't translate that to customers. @billing-bot did the reconciliation run last night?

billing-bot: System: marketplace-reconciler v2.4 ran at 2024-10-10T03:12Z. Created credit memo CM-98765 for invoice INV-20241009. Migration note: missing reseller->customer backfill for tier_id 300->315.

sasha: If AWS already applied credits to the reseller account, accounting needs a contra-revenue entry so ARR/MTD aren't overstated. Anything > $50k needs CFO sign-off per policy. @revenue-ops please advise GL mapping.

revenue-ops: Confirm policy. For marketplace-reseller retro credits use GL 4102 (marketplace_rebate) and contra entry 2010 (accrued_credit). We need: partner email thread, reconciliation CSV, and internal approval note. Please raise a ticket in Jira FIN-OPS with attachments.

noah: Done — Jira FIN-OPS-4821 created and attached CSV + S3 link. Quick query I ran to find affected invoices: 
```sql
SELECT invoice_id, SUM(charge) as net_adjust FROM invoice_lines 
WHERE partner_id = 'RESELLER-123' AND invoice_date >= '2024-10-01'
GROUP BY invoice_id HAVING ABS(SUM(charge)) > 10;
```
That returns 28 invoice_ids, total exposure $67,420.

eli: AWS tells me they sent an updated reconciliation yesterday with corrected beneficiary=RESELLER-123 -> apply to partner ledger; they also provided a CSV mapping file. We need to decide whether to: 1) reverse the $67k ledger line and re-post credits to reseller account, or 2) leave as-is and bill customers the offset (not ideal).

noah: Proposed remediation: create customer-level credit memos where negative usage lines exist, and create an offsetting journal to clear the large RESELLER line against accrued credits. Will impact revenue recognition this period. Requesting approval to proceed with option 1.

olivia: I approve proceeding to draft the journal entries and the credit memos so revenue ops can review. Hold final posting until CFO signs. @cfo can you review FIN-OPS-4821 and approve? :eyes:

cfo: Reviewing now. Need a 1-paragraph business justification and confirmation that customers will see correct invoices (no double credits). If partner confirmed corrected reconciliation, I'm inclined to approve. Please include estimated timing for posting (this month vs next).

noah: Will add justification to FIN-OPS-4821 — estimate posting in this month's close if we get signoff by EOD tomorrow. I'll add a checklist: partner email, CSV, S3 link, journal draft, impacted invoice list.

olivia: Thanks. Once CFO signs, ops can run a backfill job to remap tier_id 300->315 and re-run reconciliation for the 28 invoices. Expect a follow-up thread after posting. :thumbsup:
